title: You just got $100,000. First move?
intro: No strings, no investor, no board. What you reach for first says more than any plan you have written down.
og_line: Five questions and where the money would actually go.

results.name: Straight into marketing
results.headline: You believe the thing works, nobody knows it exists.
results.body: Your instinct is that the problem is attention rather than product, and you are often right about that.
results.cost: Paid attention stops the day the money does.

results.name: Hire someone
results.headline: You are the bottleneck and you know it.
results.body: The honest answer is that everything waits on you, and buying hands is the fastest way to stop that.
results.cost: Hiring while it is chaotic multiplies the chaos rather than dividing it.

results.name: Build the product out
results.headline: Make it good enough to sell itself.
results.body: You want to close the gap between what it is and what you promised, and you would rather do that before selling harder.
results.cost: There is no version so good that it markets itself.

results.name: Save nearly all of it
results.headline: Runway is the only real strategy.
results.body: Cash in the bank buys time, and time is what kills most of the businesses that die.
results.cost: Runway with nothing changing on it is just a slower ending.

results.name: Something you will regret
results.headline: Honest, at least.
results.body: The office, the rebrand, the setup. Everyone has one of these, and most people will not admit to it.
results.cost: You will explain this purchase to somebody in about eight months.
